1. Introduction
In a natural circulation loop, the circulating ﬂuid removes heat from a 
source and transports it to a heat sink. The driving force is the ﬂuid 
buoyancy force. In a closed loop, steady state natural circulation is 
achieved when the driving buoyancy forces are in balance with the 
frictional forces. However, under certain circumstances, the achieved 
steady state can be dynamically unstable. The possible instabilities  can
